test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: “No Improvement Required.”

The economic reforms introduced last year are __aimed at bringing up__ the overall productivity of the nation.
solution:
The correct answer is '**2**' i.e. aimed at bringing about.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The correct phrase is "**aimed at bringing about**" as it properly conveys the intention to achieve or cause a specific result.
 
• The preposition "**at**" is used to indicate the target or goal of the action, followed by "**bringing about**" to suggest bringing into existence or causing something to happen.
 
• **Options 1** and **3** are grammatically incorrect due to improper usage of prepositions and phrases.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The economic reforms introduced last year are aimed at bringing about the overall productivity of the nation."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "aimed in bringing forward" is incorrect as "in" is not the appropriate preposition for this context, and "bringing forward" does not fit the meaning intended.
 
• **Option 3:** "aimed for bringing about" is incorrect because "for" is not the correct preposition to convey the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4:** "No improvement required" is incorrect as the given sentence needs refinement for proper grammar and meaning.
